purpose: This combination medicine helps relieve symptoms of colds and allergies. It reduces fever and mild to moderate pain while also helping with sneezing, runny nose, and watery eyes. It is commonly used when you have a cold, hay fever, or other upper respiratory allergies.
how_it_works: Acetaminophen works by reducing signals in your brain that cause pain and fever, helping you feel more comfortable. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that blocks a natural substance in your body called histamine, which your body releases during an allergic reaction. Together, they tackle both the aches and the allergy or cold symptoms at the same time.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy is very common, especially from the chlorpheniramine part. You may also notice a dry mouth, dry nose, or dry throat. Some people feel dizzy, have an upset stomach, or feel a little blurry-eyed. These effects are usually mild.
warnings: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine because it increases your risk of liver damage and makes drowsiness much worse. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other products that also contain acetaminophen to prevent accidental overdose, which can seriously harm your liver. Check with your doctor first if you have liver disease, glaucoma, enlarged prostate, or breathing problems like asthma. Keep out of reach of children.
typical_dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older typically take the recommended dose every 4 to 6 hours as needed, usually no more than 4 doses in 24 hours. Always follow the directions on the package or as told by your doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than instructed, and do not use for longer than 7 days unless your doctor says so.
